subject: Environment
topic: Paris Agreement and climate negotiations — mixed tiers
description: UNFCCC, Kyoto vs Paris, NDCs, India's targets, COPs, Loss & Damage Fund

questions.stem: The Paris Agreement was adopted at the COP-21 of the UNFCCC in:
questions.explanation: Paris Agreement — adopted 12 December 2015 at COP-21 in Paris. 196 parties. Entered into force 4 November 2016 (after threshold of 55 countries representing 55% of global emissions ratified). Aims — limit global warming to 'well below 2 °C' above pre-industrial levels, with efforts to limit to 1.5 °C. Each country submits voluntary NDCs (Nationally Determined Contributions); ratchet mechanism every 5 years. India ratified on 2 October 2016 (Gandhi Jayanti).

questions.stem: Paris Agreement's main difference from the Kyoto Protocol (1997) is that:

options.option_text: Paris is non-binding for all countries
Paris uses voluntary NDCs from ALL countries (developed + developing); Kyoto bound only Annex-I (developed) countries
Kyoto was about ozone, not climate

questions.explanation: Kyoto Protocol (adopted 1997, in force 2005) — top-down legally binding emission targets only on Annex-I countries (developed). Lacked US (Senate refused) — toothless. Paris Agreement — bottom-up voluntary NDCs from EVERY party. Legally binding to SUBMIT NDCs (procedural) but the targets themselves are not legally enforceable. Includes ratchet — strengthen NDCs every 5 years; Global Stocktake every 5 years (first one concluded at COP-28, 2023). 1.5 °C goal added in 2018 IPCC SR15 → reinforced at Glasgow COP-26.

questions.stem: Under its updated NDCs (August 2022), India aims to achieve net-zero by which year?

options.option_text: 2070 (announced by PM Modi at COP-26 Glasgow, 2021)

questions.explanation: Net-zero target year — 2070 (announced at COP-26 Glasgow, 1 November 2021 by PM Modi as part of 'Panchamrit'). The other 4 commitments: (1) reach 500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030; (2) 50% of electricity from renewables by 2030; (3) reduce projected CO₂ emissions by 1 billion tonnes by 2030; (4) reduce emissions intensity of GDP by 45% from 2005 levels by 2030 (revised from 33-35%). Compare global net-zero targets — China 2060, USA 2050, EU 2050. India's later target reflects 'historical emissions equity'.

questions.stem: The Loss and Damage Fund — to compensate developing countries for irreversible climate harm — was operationalised at:
questions.explanation: L&D Fund — first agreed in principle at COP-27 (Sharm el-Sheikh, 2022) — historic decision after 30 years of demands by Vulnerable countries (V20, AOSIS). OPERATIONALISED at COP-28 (Dubai, December 2023) with initial pledges of ~$700M (UAE, Germany, EU, UK, US contributors). Hosted by World Bank as 'interim' arrangement. India + Pakistan + others demand additionality (not just rebadged climate aid). COP-28 also concluded the first Global Stocktake — finding the world is 'far off track' for 1.5 °C.

questions.stem: The Paris Agreement targets to limit global warming to:

options.option_text: Well below 2 °C, with effort to limit to 1.5 °C above pre-industrial levels

questions.explanation: Article 2 of the Paris Agreement — keep 'well below 2 °C above pre-industrial levels and pursuing efforts to limit the temperature increase to 1.5 °C'. Pre-industrial baseline = average of 1850-1900. Current warming (~2024) — ~1.3 °C above pre-industrial. The 1.5 °C threshold may be temporarily breached on annual basis as early as 2025-2026 (a single year — different from the long-term 20-year average that the Paris target uses). IPCC AR6 (2021-23) — current pace insufficient.

questions.stem: The 'Common but Differentiated Responsibilities' (CBDR) principle — central to the UNFCCC — recognises that:

options.option_text: Developed countries (Annex-I) bear greater historical responsibility and must take the lead in climate action and finance
Only the largest emitters need to act
Climate is a regional, not global, issue

questions.explanation: CBDR — formally CBDR-RC (Common But Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities). Codified in 1992 Rio UNFCCC. Acknowledges that while climate change is a common concern, developed countries (which industrialised first, releasing most cumulative emissions) bear greater obligation. India regularly invokes CBDR + 'climate justice' + 'equitable carbon space'. $100B/year climate finance pledge (Copenhagen 2009) — was meant to operationalise CBDR; still under-delivered.

questions.stem: The 'International Solar Alliance' (ISA) — initiated jointly by India and France — was launched at:

options.option_text: COP-21 Paris 2015 — by PM Modi and President Hollande

questions.explanation: ISA — co-initiated by India and France on 30 November 2015 at COP-21 Paris. Treaty-based intergovernmental organisation (only the 2nd HQed in India after the South Asian University). HQ at Gurugram, Haryana (the Solar Energy Centre). Open to all UN member states. Aim: deploy 1 TW of solar by 2030, mobilise USD 1 trillion of investment, training, R&D. India became the first signatory; the Framework Agreement opened for signature 15 November 2016. As of 2024 — 100+ member countries.
